clue.text: The point is to determine sentence

definitions.meaning: the punctuation dot at the close of a written statement
what brings a sentence to its termination, read as a description

explanation.walkthrough: 'determine' is read as de-terminate, to bring to an end: the dot is what ends a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A period mark is a point, and its job is to end a sentence of writing.

clue.text: Gives support, having risen, and doesn't give way

parts.note: something that has risen is up
to hold is to stand firm and not yield

explanation.surface: A structure that props something up, rises and refuses to buckle.
explanation.definitionFit: To uphold is to back or sustain, as a pillar bears a weight.

clue.text: Absurd old king in charge, or set up over us

parts.note: King Lud is a legendary early king of Britain, remembered in Ludgate

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the little word is written bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ridiculous ancient monarch is in command, or placed above us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns OR into RO; 'over' simply puts US below it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludicrous and absurd are synonyms for something laughably unreasonable.

clue.text: One of these might be thrown in at a loss

definitions.text: One of these might be thrown in at a loss

parts.words: One of these might be thrown in at a loss
parts.note: a boxer's corner tosses a drying cloth into the ring to concede, and the idiom 'throw in the towel' means give up when losing

explanation.definitionFit: Bath cloths are what a beaten boxer's second throws into the ring to surrender.

clue.text: The story of an outlandish plight

parts.note: peregrine once meant foreign, from abroad, hence outlandish
to be in a pickle is to be in a sorry plight

explanation.surface: A tale about someone caught in a bizarre predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: The story is Tobias Smollett's 1751 novel The Adventures of Peregrine Pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Peregrine Pickle is the title of an eighteenth-century picaresque novel, so it names a story.

clue.text: Tease someone on a diet

definitions.meaning: a follower of William Banting's nineteenth-century slimming regime was called a ...

explanation.walkthrough: Banting was a Victorian low-carbohydrate diet, named after the undertaker who popularised it.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful teasing is chaff, and a Banting dieter was once nicknamed this.

clue.text: Management institute, note, has perhaps one Turkish officer

parts.note: BIM was the British Institute of Management
B is a musical note

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the little word are one possible arrangement, so shuffle them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A business school and a memo together produce a military man from Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges HAS into ASH. The usual spelling is binbashi; the setter uses the variant with M.
explanation.definitionFit: A bimbashi was a major in the Ottoman army, a rank of Turkish officer.

clue.text: There is shortly a saint to be named

parts.note: there is shortened to the contraction there's

explanation.surface: Someone announces that a holy person is about to be identified.
explanation.walkthrough: St Theresa (Teresa of Avila) is the saint; 'to be named' says the answer is her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is the given name of the Spanish mystic canonised as a saint.

clue.text: They could give Dowson the wherewithal for a fling

definitions.text: They could give Dowson the wherewithal for a fling

parts.words: They could give Dowson the wherewithal for a fling
parts.note: the poet Ernest Dowson wrote in Cynara of flinging roses riotously with the throng, so bushes bearing those blooms supply what he flung

explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' suggests a spree; in Dowson's poem it is the act of throwing flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushes bearing roses supply the flowers Dowson's speaker flung.

clue.text: Follow announcement in theatrical entertainment

indicators.note: in places the notice inside the stage production

parts.note: a stage show
an ad is an advertisement, a public announcement

explanation.surface: Keep up with the news given out during a stage performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to tail them closely, following unseen.

clue.text: House-to house delivery men

parts.note: reads like door-to-door postmen, but means people who carry a household's furniture from one home to the next

explanation.definitionFit: Furniture movers take everything from the old home and deliver it to the new one.

clue.text: He is not strikingly agreeable to his colleagues

definitions.text: He is not strikingly agreeable to his colleagues

parts.words: He is not strikingly agreeable to his colleagues
parts.note: strikingly suggests very, but means as regards a strike: he will not join his fellow workers' walkout

explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker works on while fellow workers are out, so he disagrees with them over striking.

clue.text: Mark of grave stress perhaps

definitions.meaning: a grave is a written diacritic sign over a vowel
emphasis laid on a syllable in speech is one example

explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a tomb or solemn, but it is the backward-sloping sign over a letter, as in à.
explanation.definitionFit: The grave is a diacritic sign, and spoken emphasis on a syllable is also called this.

clue.text: Wild coast for a royal meeting

indicators.note: wild tells us the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A rugged shoreline makes the setting for a gathering of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is the racecourse in Berkshire whose June race meeting is Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Ascot is a famous horse-racing fixture attended by the monarch.

clue.text: Sword-taps heard tonight ?

parts.note: the touches of a blade on the shoulder when a man is dubbed a knight; heard puns on to knight

explanation.walkthrough: 'tonight' is heard as 'to knight': the taps are given to make a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade was the ceremonial touch of a sword conferring knighthood.

clue.text: Go angling on river with something to hold lines together

parts.note: to fish is to go angling
the River Plate is the estuary between Argentina and Uruguay

explanation.surface: A fisherman heads to the water, taking gear to keep his lines tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' suggests fishing lines; they are railway lines, whose rails are bolted end to end by this plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishplate is a metal bar bolted across the joint of two railway rails.

clue.text: Omits evidence of spring

definitions.meaning: when a tree puts out its new foliage in the season after winter

explanation.definitionFit: To exclude something is to drop it, and a tree in bud putting out foliage signals spring.

clue.text: Paying no attention to Deputy-Head is characteristic

indicators.note: head, attached to Deputy by the hyphen, asks for the opening letter of that word

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: Ignoring the deputy head is typical behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrait means absent-minded, distracted by worry.

clue.text: Study features of church building plots

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
spires are tall pointed features of a church

explanation.surface: Someone surveys the architecture of a church, then the burial plots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plots' looks like plots of land beside a church; it is a verb, schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to scheme secretly, which is what plotting means.

clue.text: Billy-boys from France

parts.note: the men who crossed from France with William the Conqueror in 1066, Billy being short for William

explanation.definitionFit: William's invading army of 1066 were the men from Normandy.

clue.text: Whereby the power of a painter is measured ?

definitions.text: Whereby the power of a painter is measured ?

parts.words: Whereby the power of a painter is measured ?
parts.note: electrical power is measured in units named after James Watt

explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of power shares its plural with the surname of the painter George Frederic Watts.

clue.text: Comparatively neat clue for Halifax ?

definitions.meaning: more tidy, the comparative of a word for neat
George Savile, Marquess of Halifax, was nicknamed for his political middle course and wrote The Character of a ..., so the nickname hints at him

explanation.walkthrough: Halifax is not the Yorkshire town but the 17th-century statesman who defended trimming between parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidier is the comparative of neat, and a politician who shifts between sides is a time-server, Halifax's nickname.

clue.text: Fix pleats perhaps of woollen fibre

indicators.note: fix as in rearrange: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Secure the folds, perhaps, of a woollen garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like a definition (it is one sense of the answer), but here it rearranges PLEATS; 'perhaps' marks the anagram as one option.
explanation.definitionFit: Staple is the fibre of wool or cotton judged by its length and quality.

clue.text: Officer with song in his heart-—or the makings of a neat catch

definitions.text: the makings of a neat catch

indicators.note: the song sits in the centre of the officer, between his letters

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: An officer with a melody in mind, or the means to make a tidy capture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, rope with a running noose used to rope cattle.

clue.text: "Fearless" I misprinted

annotationWithheld.why: "Fearless" I misprinted (8): the only parse is I + PRINTED rearranged, where the single word 'misprinted' gives both the anagram signal (mis-) and the fodder PRINTED, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: A snag for a ward

parts.note: the letters of draw read backwards spell ward

explanation.surface: A problem facing a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a disadvantage or hitch.

clue.text: Introductions required for printers' units

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
an em is a printer's unit of measure

explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a preface or prelude to a book or speech.

clue.text: Twice set about finishing sonnet

indicators.note: about here means turned around and mixed, so the letters are rearranged
twice asks for the word set to be written two times over before shuffling

explanation.surface: Setting down the end of a sonnet two times.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestet is the closing six-line section of a Petrarchan sonnet.

clue.text: German princes choose alternative quarter

parts.note: to elect is to choose
or introduces an alternative
S, south, is a compass quarter

explanation.surface: Royalty of Germany pick another district.
explanation.walkthrough: The Electors were the princes of the Holy Roman Empire entitled to elect the Emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Roman Empire's prince-electors chose the Emperor.
